sentence:
Recall that the translation Tₖ defined by
  Tₖ(x) = x + k
has a well‐known cycle structure when acting as a permutation on ℤ:
 • If k = 0, then T₀ is the identity.
sentence-category-reason: Recalls the definition and basic property (cycle structure) of translations on ℤ.

sentence: • If k ≠ 0, then Tₖ breaks ℤ into |k| disjoint orbits (each given by a congruence class modulo |k|); each orbit is an infinite cycle.
sentence-category-reason: States the orbit structure for nonzero translations; theoretical property.

Now, since f ∘ g and g ∘ f are “conjugate” (indeed, if f is an invertible function then
  g ∘ f = f⁻¹ ∘ (f ∘ g) ∘ f),
they must have the same cycle structure.
sentence-category-reason: Uses conjugacy to deduce same cycle structure; logical inference.

sentence: In particular, they must have the same number of orbits.
sentence-category-reason: Draws a specific consequence of having the same cycle structure.

sentence: But the number of orbits of f ∘ g is |a| while that of g ∘ f is |b|.
sentence-category-reason: Identifies the number of orbits for each composition based on earlier facts.
